findings.label: Paid During Active Breaches
findings.detail: 1 suppliers received payments while in breach of Companies Act — including 0 critical and 0 high severity. Temporally verified against payment dates.

findings.label: Likely Duplicate Payments
findings.detail: 17076 high-confidence duplicate groups with same supplier, amount, date and reference (3+ copies) (after filtering 63774 CSV republication artifacts)
findings.context_note: Quarterly CSV overlaps (same transaction appearing in 2 files) have been filtered out. Remaining duplicates show 3+ identical copies, which are more likely genuine overpayments.

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 2387 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 7871 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Year-End Spending Pattern
findings.detail: Law & Governance spent 3.8x their monthly average in March (£106.0K above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
findings.context_note: March spending above the monthly average is expected for UK councils on April–March fiscal years. Compare against prior years' March figures for meaningful analysis.

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Rugby Care Centre (2.0 day avg, 11 payments, £17.4K)

findings.label: Benford's Law Analysis
findings.detail: Digit distribution across 1,128,142 transactions shows χ²=41974.74 (statistically significant due to large sample size), but max digit deviation is only 4.1% — within the normal range for UK council spending patterns. No practical evidence of fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 1,128,142+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (4.1%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 1,133,973 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 0 deviates 1.58% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=1,133,973.

findings.label: Weak Competition Indicators
findings.detail: 2 contracts show signs of limited competition (short tender periods or rapid award). Top: WCC - Dynamic Purchasing System for Ice Cream Conc (£237.0K)
findings.context_note: Contracts Finder does not publish bid counts. These flags use proxy signals: tender periods under 14 days and awards within 7 days of deadline. Short timelines may have legitimate explanations (framework call-offs, urgency).

key_findings.title: 10 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: County Cars 2003 Ltd — every 2.0 days (29 payments, £80.4K)

key_findings.title: PERTEMPS RECRUITMENT PARTNERSHIP LTD: 57487 transactions totalling £72.4M
key_findings.description: Averaging £1.3K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier

key_findings.title: AI DOGE covers 23% of £989.1M GOV.UK outturn
key_findings.description: Spending >£500 threshold means smaller transactions are excluded. Largest gaps: Education services, Highways and transport services, Children Social Care. This is expected — not a data quality issue.
